speaker: Doctor
text:
I have noted your recent high fever and seizure. To better understand the cause of your generalized nonpruritic rash, have you noticed any specific pattern, such as the rash spreading from your trunk to your extremities or appearing in a "bull's-eye" shape?

Also, when did these symptoms begin, and have you experienced any joint pain, headache, or sensitivity to light since the fever started?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)

REQUEST IMAGES: None needed at this time; clinical presentation is classic for this viral exanthem caused by HHV-6 or HHV-7. I am confident in this diagnosis given the high fever preceding the rash by several days, the age of the infant, and the absence of other systemic symptoms like photophobia or significant joint pain. Have you noticed any signs of dehydration or difficulty breathing in addition to the fever and seizure?
